content.title: Jason Day majors timeline: Inside the golfer's last major win and more | Sporting News
content.text: Jason Day has been a professional golfer for about 15 years. He debuted at the Masters in 2011 and impressed everyone when he finished tied for second. This set unrealistic expectations, but Day has still been able to pick up a win at a golf major so far in his career. The Australian golfer has gone viral for the outfits that he wears when playing. He is a big bird-watcher, and some of his polos have been adorned with colorful birds to show off his hobby. Day has never been shy about showing off his personality while on the Tour. Fans have come to enjoy his interviews, learning more about his background and career. Day hasn't had sustained success over the course of his career, but has still turned in some memorable performances at the golf majors. Here is more on how Day has done at the golf majors in his career. SN's MASTERS HQ: Live Masters leaderboard | Masters TV coverage | Live streamingHas Jason Day won a major?Yes. Day currently has one major win on his resume. He won the 2015 PGA Championship with an impressive score of 20-under. Day beat out the runner-up Jordan Spieth by two strokes. He had the third-best score in the first round with a 4-under 68. Day improved on the second day and had a 67 to move to 9-under. He took the lead on the leaderboard on Day 3 and shot a 66 to move to 15-under. Day's final round of 67 clinched the victory for him. LIVE: 2026 Masters scores, results and highlightsHow old is Jason Day?Day was born on November 12, 1987 and is 38 years old. He was born in Beaudesert, Queensland, Australia and remained in Australia throughout his amateur career, first leaving the country when he turned professional. Day now has a residence in Australia and another in Ohio. LIVE: Tracking the 2026 Masters cut lineJason Day Masters historyDay has yet to earn his first green jacket. In 2011, he finished second alongside fellow Aussie Adam Scott at 12-under. The pair finished just behind Charl Schwartzel who won the event at 14-under. Day's rounds went 72-64-72-68, with his second day being an outlier. He wasn't able to re-create that success over the other three days, but still played well enough to finish tied for second.
